chapters.title: Chapter 1: How Income Tax in India Is Structured

lessons.title: What a Tax Slab Is: Progressive Taxation Explained

body.text: A slab rate applies only to the rupees that fall inside that slab. Crossing into a higher slab never raises the tax on the income you already had.

markDefs.definition: A band of income that is taxed at one fixed rate. Your income is split across several slabs, and each portion is taxed at the rate of the slab it falls into.

children.text: Ask ten salaried people in Bengaluru or Pune what "being in the 30% bracket" means and most will say it means 30% of their salary goes to the government. It does not. Indian income tax is built on
, and once you understand how slabs actually work, every other topic in this course, from the rebate to surcharge, becomes simple arithmetic.

There are two basic ways a government can tax income. A flat tax charges everyone the same percentage. A progressive tax charges higher rates as income rises, but only on the additional income. India, like most large economies, taxes individuals progressively. The idea is ability to pay: the rupee that buys groceries is taxed lightly or not at all, while the rupee that funds a second holiday is taxed more.

columns.label: Flat Tax
points: One rate for every rupee of income, for everyone
A clerk earning 5 lakh and a CXO earning 5 crore pay the same percentage
Takes a bigger bite, proportionally, out of lower incomes that go mostly on essentials
Not used for individual income tax in India

columns.label: Progressive (Slab) Tax
points: Income is split into bands, each with its own rate
The lowest band is taxed at 0%
Higher rates apply only to income above each threshold
The share of income paid as tax rises gradually, never in sudden jumps
The system India uses for individuals under both the new and old regimes

children.text: The Slab Table You Will Use Most

markDefs.definition: The level of income up to which no tax is charged. Under the new regime for individuals it is 4 lakh; under the old regime it is 2.5 lakh for most individuals below 60.

children.text: The new tax regime is the default for individuals, and its slabs are set out in section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 115BAC of the Income-tax Act, 1961). The first 4 lakh is the
. After that, the rate climbs by 5 percentage points every 4 lakh until it reaches 30%. The old regime has its own, shorter table, which Chapter 2 covers in detail.

body.caption: New Tax Regime Slabs for Individuals, Tax Year 2026-27

body.text: Slabs are applied to taxable income, not to your CTC or gross salary. Standard deduction and other adjustments come off first (Lesson 3 of this chapter). The rebate and the 4% cess are applied after the slab tax is worked out (Chapter 3). In this lesson we focus only on the slab step itself.

children.text: Worked Example: Priya's Taxable Income of 18 Lakh

Priya is a product analyst in Gurugram with taxable income of ₹18,00,000 under the new regime. Her top slab is 20%. The wrong calculation is 18 lakh × 20% = ₹3,60,000. The right calculation fills each slab in turn, like pouring water into a row of buckets: the first bucket fills, then the overflow spills into the next.

body.caption: Priya's Slab Tax, Bucket by Bucket

body.title: Where Priya's ₹1,60,000 of Slab Tax Comes From

children.text: The general formula is the same for any income and either regime: multiply the income inside each slab by that slab's rate, then add the results.

body.latex: \text{Slab Tax} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i \times \text{Income falling in slab } i
body.caption: r is the rate of each slab; slabs above your income contribute zero

body.text: Multiplying your whole income by your top slab rate is the single most common slab mistake. For Priya it overstates her slab tax by ₹2,00,000, more than double the real figure. If an app, a relative or a colleague quotes a tax number that looks like income × top rate, it is wrong.

body.title: Show me the math: taxable income of 25 lakh

children.text: At ₹25,00,000 every slab is used, including the 30% slab. First 4 lakh: ₹0. Next 4 lakh at 5%: ₹20,000. Next 4 lakh at 10%: ₹40,000. Next 4 lakh at 15%: ₹60,000. Next 4 lakh at 20%: ₹80,000. Next 4 lakh at 25%: ₹1,00,000. The remaining ₹1,00,000 above 24 lakh at 30%: ₹30,000. Total slab tax: ₹3,30,000, which is 13.2% of income, even though this person is "in the 30% bracket".

body.title: Recent Milestones in the Individual Slab System

events.title: New Regime Introduced
events.description: The Finance Act, 2020 created an optional new regime with lower rates in 2.5 lakh steps, in exchange for giving up most deductions. The old regime remained the default.

events.title: New Regime Becomes the Default
events.description: From FY 2023-24 the new regime became the default, the basic exemption limit rose to 3 lakh and the 50,000 standard deduction was extended to it.

events.title: Slabs Widened, Standard Deduction Raised
events.description: The July 2024 Budget widened the new regime slabs and raised the standard deduction for salaried taxpayers to 75,000.

events.title: The 4 Lakh Staircase
events.description: The February 2025 Budget reset the new regime slabs to equal 4 lakh steps with a 4 lakh exemption limit, and raised the rebate so that taxable income up to 12 lakh attracts no tax.

events.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 Takes Effect
events.description: The new Act replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the "previous year" and "assessment year" with a single "tax year". The slab structure itself carried over.

body.title: Slab Tax at 10 Lakh
body.question: Ananya has taxable income of ₹10,00,000 under the new regime. Before any rebate or cess, which statement about her slab tax is correct?
options: Her full ₹10,00,000 is taxed at 10%, so slab tax is ₹1,00,000
First ₹4,00,000 at nil, next ₹4,00,000 at 5% and the last ₹2,00,000 at 10%, so slab tax is ₹40,000
Most of her income sits in the 5% slab, so it is all taxed at 5%, giving ₹50,000
Her income is below 12 lakh, so slab tax is zero
body.explanation: ₹0 + ₹20,000 + ₹20,000 = ₹40,000. Option D confuses two separate steps. The rebate covered in Chapter 3 will wipe out Ananya's final tax bill, but the slab calculation still produces ₹40,000 first. The rebate is then applied against that figure.

body.title: Calculate the Slab Tax
body.prompt: Karthik, a software engineer in Chennai, has taxable income of ₹14,00,000 under the new regime. What is his slab tax, before rebate and cess?
body.explanation: Up to 4 lakh: ₹0. 4 to 8 lakh at 5%: ₹20,000. 8 to 12 lakh at 10%: ₹40,000. The remaining ₹2,00,000 between 12 and 14 lakh at 15%: ₹30,000. Total: ₹90,000, which is about 6.4% of his income.

body.title: The Core Rule
body.textWithBlank: In a progressive slab system, a higher rate applies only to the portion of income ___ the slab threshold.
body.explanation: Income below each threshold keeps being taxed at the lower rates. That is why moving into a higher slab can never make the tax on your earlier income go up.

body.title: The Raise Rohan Almost Turned Down
body.scenario: Rohan works at a Mumbai fintech. His taxable income is ₹16,00,000 under the new regime. His manager offers a raise that takes it to ₹17,00,000. A colleague warns him: "Don't take it. You'll move into the 20% slab and pay 20% on your whole salary. That's ₹3,40,000 in tax."
body.prompt: Is the colleague right? Work out how much extra tax the raise actually costs Rohan and how much of the ₹1,00,000 he keeps. Include the 4% cess on the extra tax.
body.modelAnswer: The colleague is wrong. Only the ₹1,00,000 above 16 lakh is taxed at 20%, adding ₹20,000 of slab tax. Slab tax goes from ₹1,20,000 (₹20,000 + ₹40,000 + ₹60,000) to ₹1,40,000, not ₹3,40,000. With 4% cess the extra tax is ₹20,000 + ₹800 = ₹20,800, so Rohan keeps ₹79,200 of the raise. At this income level, a raise never leaves you with less money than before.

cards.definition: A band of income taxed at one fixed rate, such as 8 to 12 lakh at 10% under the new regime.
A system where rates rise with income, but each higher rate applies only to income above its threshold.
A single rate applied to all income. Not used for individual income tax in India.
The income level up to which the tax rate is nil. 4 lakh under the new regime for individuals.
The rate of the highest slab your income reaches. It applies only to the income inside that slab.
The tax produced by applying slab rates to taxable income, before the rebate, surcharge and cess.

points: India taxes individual income progressively, using slabs with rising rates
Each slab rate applies only to the income that falls inside that slab
Under the new regime for tax year 2026-27, the rate rises by 5 points every 4 lakh, from nil up to 4 lakh to 30% above 24 lakh
Slab tax is worked out bucket by bucket, never as total income × top rate
A taxpayer in the 20% or 30% slab pays far less than 20% or 30% of income overall
Slabs apply to taxable income; the rebate, surcharge and cess come after the slab step

body.text: Slab rates in this lesson are for resident individuals under the new tax regime for tax year 2026-27 under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Rates can change in each Union Budget. This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice. Verify current rates on incometax.gov.in before filing.
